name: Mobbin
subcategory: UI pattern and flow reference library
tagline: A searchable library of real app screenshots and user flows, captured and tagged by hand for design reference.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The software part of Mobbin is a tagged image database with a nice grid and a filter sidebar, which any competent agent can produce in an afternoon. The product is not the software. It is tens of thousands of screens captured from real apps, organized into coherent flows, re-captured every time those apps redesign, and labeled with a consistent taxonomy of patterns, elements and industries. You cannot one-shot that, and you cannot scrape it either without inheriting both a legal problem and a staleness problem. A personal version is only useful for screenshots you already collect yourself, which is a different and much smaller thing.
coreLoopDIY: A local screenshot library where you drop images, group them into named flows, tag them, and filter or full-text search the result.
requirements: Optional: an OpenAI API key in .env if you want auto-tagging of dropped screenshots
whatYouLose: The actual corpus: thousands of apps captured screen by screen, which is the entire reason anyone opens Mobbin
Flows, not just screens: onboarding and checkout captured in order, so you can see decisions rather than isolated pretty pictures
Freshness: apps redesign and Mobbin re-shoots them, your folder rots the day you stop feeding it
A consistent taxonomy someone else maintained, so searching 'empty state' actually returns empty states
Web, iOS and Android coverage side by side for the same product
moatNotes: The capture pipeline is unglamorous manual labor at scale: install the app, walk the flow, shoot every screen, tag it, then do it again after the next release. That is the product.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the alternative is opening fifteen apps on your phone and screenshotting them yourself while trying to remember what a good referral flow looks like. Designers pay Mobbin to skip the archaeology: one search returns forty real, shipped, current examples of the exact pattern they are about to design, across platforms, in order. The price is trivially less than the hours it replaces, and no personal folder of saved screenshots ever reaches the density where search becomes useful.
notes: The grid is an afternoon, the library is a decade of manual capture. The moat is a hand-shot, hand-tagged, continuously refreshed corpus of real shipped screens that nobody can scrape into existence.
prompt:
Build a local-first personal UI reference library called "Shelf". Single user, runs on my machine, no accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, no substitutions: Next.js 15 App Router with TypeScript, Tailwind, better-sqlite3 for storage, local filesystem for image files. Everything in one repo, started with `npm run dev`.

Data model:
- app: id, name, platform (ios | android | web), notes
- flow: id, app_id, name (e.g. "Onboarding"), position
- screen: id, flow_id, file_path, position, caption, ocr_text
- tag: id, label, kind (pattern | element | industry)
- screen_tag join table

Features, in scope:
1. Drag and drop one or many images onto the page. Files are copied into ./library/<app-slug>/ and rows are inserted. Never mutate the original files.
2. An import screen where I assign the dropped batch to an app and a flow, then reorder screens by dragging.
3. A masonry grid browse view with a left filter sidebar: platform, app, tag kind then tag, plus a text box that searches captions and ocr_text via SQLite FTS5.
4. A flow view: horizontal scroll of screens in order, arrow keys to move, Escape to exit.
5. Click any screen for a lightbox with caption editing and a tag input with autocomplete over existing tags.
6. Seed the tag table with about forty common labels (onboarding, empty state, paywall, search, settings, toast, bottom sheet, stepper, and so on).

Optional and off by default: if OPENAI_API_KEY exists in .env, add a "suggest tags" button per screen that sends the image to a vision model and returns three to six suggested tags plus extracted text, which I accept or reject. If the key is absent, hide the button entirely. Never call the network otherwise.

Out of scope: scraping anything, multi-user, auth, hosted deploy, mobile app, payment.

Include a README that says plainly this is a shelf for screenshots I collect myself and is not a substitute for a curated corpus. Add a seed script that generates three fake apps with placeholder images so the UI is not empty on first run.
